study_identification_part.si4_title: Extreme deviations from the normative model reveal cortical heterogeneity and associations with negative symptom severity in first-episode psychosis from the OPTiMiSE and GAP studies

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract explicitly states the aims: apply normative modeling of cortical thickness in first-episode psychosis to quantify heterogeneity and to test whether baseline deviation patterns predict symptoms and treatment response over follow-up periods.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We applied normative modelling of cortical thickness to a sample of first-episode psychosis patients, with the aim of quantifying heterogeneity and to use any pattern of cortical atypicality to predict symptoms and response to antipsychotic medication at timepoints from baseline up to 95 weeks (median follow-ups = 4).

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: An existing normative model was used; the original reference model is cited and described (n≈37,126; 79 scanners; hierarchical Bayesian regression). Adaptation used 50% of local controls per site (OPTIMISE) with further adjustments to represent older ages in GAP. Image quality control and exclusions are reported. However, detailed eligibility criteria for the large reference cohort are not provided within this paper, and final counts of adaptation controls are not enumerated here.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: We used a pre-estimated multi-site reference normative model ... built from healthy participant data (n = 37,126) across 79 scanners ... Participant sex and scanner site have been accounted for ... the parameters of this reference normative model were adapted to the new sites with 50% of control participant data from each clinical site from the OPTiMiSE sample ... Both GAP and OPTiMiSE T1-weighted images were visually inspected ... and 21 images were excluded due to poor image quality. A further 4 patient images were excluded due to a lack of control data for that site.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age is the primary predictor in the reference model; sex and site are modeled as batch effects/hierarchical levels to remove nuisance variance. The abstract also notes accounting for gender and site effects when adapting the model.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: An existing normative model of cortical thickness (n = 37,126) was adapted to integrate data from each clinical site and account for effects of gender and site. ... Participant sex and scanner site have been accounted for in the model by inclusion as batch effects which can be interpreted as levels in multi-level modelling, enabling nuisance variance related to site and sex to be removed.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The paper explains deviation scores as z-scores relative to the normative distribution, defines extreme deviations with a quantitative threshold (|z| ≥ 2.6), and discusses clinical implications by linking baseline deviations to medium-term negative symptoms.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: For each individual, the 148 cortical thickness features were mapped to centiles of the normative distribution and converted to z-scores reflecting the distance from the population mean. Individual cortical thickness metrics of +/-2.6 standard deviations from the mean were considered extreme deviations from the norm. ... linear mixed-effects modelling showed that negative deviations ... at baseline are related to more severe negative symptoms over the medium-term.
